thread:
jamie: Customer reporting intermittent OAuth failure after clicking enterprise SSO link. They see \"state mismatch\" during callback. Happening for both GitHub and Google flows behind their link-shortener + corporate proxy. Need triage.
ingrid: Do we have a sample failing URL or trace from the customer's browser?

jamie: Pasting sanitized example and proxy log (customer says repro ~30% of clicks):

jamie: ```https://app.customer.example/callback?code=SplxlOBeZQQYbYS6WxSbIA&state=orig-state-123&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.redwood.ai%2Fauth%2Fgithub%2Fcallback```

jamie: Proxy log snippet for same request: ```GET /callback?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.redwood.ai%2Fauth%2Fgithub%2Fcallback&state=proxy-state-zzzz&code=SplxlOBeZQQYbYS6WxSbIA 200ms 302 -> https://auth.redwood.ai/cb?state=orig-state-123```

jamie: TL;DR: link-shortener creates a deeplink with state=orig-state-123, corporate proxy re-appends a state param (proxy-state-zzzz) during rewrite. On our side the server receives duplicate state parameters and ends up validating against the wrong one.

frank: Yikes. We canonicalize `state` by taking first occurrence (parsed order), but some clients/servers pick last. If proxy swaps param order, the code_verifier in session (cookie) and the state we store don't line up -> mismatch.

maria: Could be cookie scoping + path rewrite too. If the proxy strips cookie attributes or routes to a different backend, session cookie might be missing and server rejects the state. Any `Set-Cookie` in logs?

jamie: Customer attached intercepted requests — sometimes cookie present, sometimes not (race). When cookie missing we still see two `state` params. Example header capture: ```GET /callback?... HTTP/1.1
Host: app.customer.example
Cookie: session=abc123; Path=/; HttpOnly
X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3
```

ingrid: Repro steps I can run locally? If we curl the callback with two state params, does our handler error the same?

frank: Yes. Quick repro:```curl -v \"https://auth.redwood.ai/cb?state=proxy-state-zzzz&state=orig-state-123&code=...\" -b \"session=abc123\"``` Server log: `oauth: state validation failed: expected orig-state-123 got proxy-state-zzzz`

frank: Workaround options: 1) accept either state if session exists and code_verifier matches (looser validation), 2) prefer last param instead of first (but could regress other customers), 3) reject duplicate states and surface clearer telemetry.
maria: We should not weaken validation broadly. Option: detect duplicate `state` and log full raw querystring + upstream `Via` headers, then surface to customer so their proxy vendor can fix. Also add a per-tenant toggle to accept last param for enterprise accounts behind known proxies.
jamie: Customer wants a short-term fix — they asked if we can normalize by deduping and preferring the one that matches session state when present.
frank: Implementing a small guard: if duplicate `state` params exist, check session store for expected state and use that for validation (if session present). If no session, fail hard. That preserves security. I can PR a patch to auth service to do that and add telemetry.
ingrid: Please include a debug flag to log both querystring and parsed params for 24h for their tenant only. We'll need SRE approval for elevated logs.
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-114 (customer: AcmeCorp). Assigning to frank, jamie.

frank: I'll open PR now and add tests replicating `state` duplication + missing cookie cases. Target: deploy to canary tonight.
maria: I'll check ingress/CDN rules to see if we can detect common proxies that append params (some link shorteners rewrite and append UTM/state). If we can identify, we email customers with mitigation steps (configure shortener to preserve params or use fragment-based state).

jamie: Action items: frank -> auth guard + telemetry PR, ingrid -> tenant-scoped debug window, maria -> ingress probe + list of known proxies, jamie -> update customer with workaround (direct link) and ETA.

ingrid: Thanks — please paste PR link when ready and I'll review fast. :thumbsup:
